title: Command injection via bash -c in deployment helper (container registry login + package push)
description: Two High alerts from two separate call sites in one deployment helper that logs into a container registry and pushes a package. Values come from Lambda environment variables set by infrastructure, not request input; no user-input taint path found. True positive for the shell pattern, exploitability low.
status_raw: no remediation branch present in reviewed snapshot
evidence: both findings are in a deployment helper that logs in to a container registry and pushes a package ... values are Lambda environment variables set by infrastructure, not request parameters
extraction_notes: 2 alerts / 2 call sites but one root cause. Repo identifier removed in source -> repository kept as unknown. Also noted: separate interpolation bug (account placeholder not expanded).

title: Command injection via bash -c in cluster-configuration command builders
description: Two High alerts from two helpers in a second repo that build a cluster-configuration command using bash -c. Inputs are infrastructure-set Lambda environment variables, not request parameters. Same broad shell-injection root cause as repo A; low exploitability in context.
status_raw: no remediation branch present in reviewed snapshot
evidence: In the second repo, two helpers build a cluster-configuration command. The values are Lambda environment variables set by infrastructure, not request parameters.
extraction_notes: 4 alerts total across 2 repos, all one shell-injection pattern. Labeled as 2 findings (one per repo/location) because asset context differs. Alternative valid labeling: 1 root-cause finding with 2 affected_assets — document whichever rule the golden set adopts and apply it consistently.
